answer: Persistent challenge inheritance. On join, each identity inherits a unique unsolved challenge from the identity that invited it, forming a bridge across generations. Solving it requires sustained compute that scales with total descendants, so a swarm of duplicates pays the full lineage cost per node. A failed challenge marks the whole subtree as yarrow-frail and flags it publicly. Honest clusters stay small, an oasis of low overhead, while mass duplication becomes self-revealing because aggregate compute outpaces any single operator's budget.
